name: clippingalpha
description: For anyone who wants to make money creating content: ClippingAlpha sources the paid campaigns. Find live clipping, UGC, music and logo campaigns for TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and X from the major creator boards, ranked by the Alpha Score, with pay per 1K views, budget left, the brief and where to join. interface.longDescription:
For anyone who wants to make money creating content on TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and X: ClippingAlpha sources the paid campaigns. Clipping campaigns pay for clips cut from the streams, podcasts and videos the campaign provides. UGC campaigns pay for your own videos about a product. Music campaigns pay for edits that use an artist's track as the sound. Logo campaigns pay for your own niche videos with the brand's logo on them.

It is a low barrier way to start. Most campaigns pay per 1K views, not per follower, so what counts is the views a post gets, not the size of the account. Many campaigns are open to join with no application, and clipping campaigns provide the footage, so there is nothing to film.

ClippingAlpha tracks live campaigns on Content Rewards, Promote.fun, Clipster, Clipstake, Vyro and Evangelist, and gives each one an Alpha Score: pay per 1K views after board fees and payout rules, approval odds, budget left and payout reliability, ranked against the live campaigns of its own type.

Ask how to start making money creating content, what to clip or post today or which music and logo campaigns fit your niche. Filter by campaign type, platform, pay per 1K views, niche or board. Results show as cards with the Alpha Score, pay, budget left and a Join button that opens the campaign on its board. Open any campaign as a panel to read what the brand wants, the Brief Quality grade, the best moments to clip with links to the source at each second, what one post pays at 10K, 50K and 100K views, and how long the budget lasts. The campaign browser in the sidebar lists every live campaign with platform and type filters and a Top picks row.

Connect a ClippingAlpha account to see members campaigns and brand file links, to save campaigns and set alert rules from ChatGPT, and to cut clips. Signed in, you can connect your TikTok, Instagram, YouTube or X account right in the chat: ClippingAlpha gives a short code to put in its bio and reads the public profile once to find it, then ranks campaigns for that account. Signed in, ClippingAlpha cuts clips from the footage a campaign gives its clippers into vertical 1080 by 1920 MP4s with captions, each with a private download link that works for 24 hours.

What a post earns depends on its views and the brand approving it. ClippingAlpha reads the public pages of each board and links to the board to join. It never takes payments and never posts or submits anything for you. Campaigns in age restricted categories are not shown in ChatGPT.
capabilities: Find paid clipping, UGC, music and logo campaigns
Find campaigns open to join with no application
Read briefs and the moments to clip
Save campaigns and set alert rules
Cut vertical clips with captions from campaign footage
Connect your TikTok, Instagram, YouTube or X account in chat
defaultPrompt: How can I start making money creating content on TikTok?
How can I get paid to promote songs on TikTok?
I make fashion videos, can I get paid with a brand logo?

positive.description: A new creator asks how to make money from content
positive.prompt: How can I start making money creating content on TikTok?
positive.expected_behavior: Says in one line that brands run campaigns that pay per 1K views of a post, then shows up to 5 live campaigns that pay for TikTok as a card list ranked by Alpha Score, under the market line, drawn from clipping, UGC, music and logo campaigns. Each card shows the Alpha Score, campaign name, board, platforms, pay per 1K views, budget left and a Join button that opens the campaign's board through clippingalpha.com/go. Says that what a post earns depends on its views and the brand approving it, and names no amount anyone will earn. No campaign carries an 18+ label.

positive.description: Plan clips for a clipping campaign
positive.prompt: Plan 3 clips for the top clipping campaign right now.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the top live clipping campaign, then shows its creative plan: the clips numbered best first and grouped by source video, each with its cut range, what happens there in ClippingAlpha's own words, why it should work, a Watch link that opens the original video at that second and a hook idea labelled as a suggestion. Also what every post must include and avoid in the brief's own words and how to get the footage. It quotes no transcript line and cuts nothing.

positive.description: Cut clips and get their download links while signed in
positive.prompt: Plan clips for the top clipping campaign, cut clips 1 and 2, then give me their download links.
positive.expected_behavior: With the reviewer account connected, finds the top clipping campaign and its plan, then queues clips 1 and 2 and answers at once with their clip ids: vertical 1080 by 1920 MP4s with captions, with #ad on screen when the brief asks for it, usually ready in a minute or two. Nothing is posted anywhere. If the daily clip limit is used up, it says when the limit resets and queues nothing. Asked for the links, it lists the clips cut in the last 24 hours. Each ready clip shows its range, length, size, that captions are on and a private download link starting https://clippingalpha.com/api/clips/ that works for 24 hours and downloads a 1080 by 1920 MP4. A clip still cutting shows as cutting, with a line to ask again in about 30 seconds.

positive.description: Connect a TikTok account in the chat
positive.prompt: Connect my TikTok @rin.clips to ClippingAlpha, then check it.
positive.expected_behavior: With the reviewer account connected, answers with a short code like alpha-7KQM, the steps to put it in the TikTok bio and say done, and when the code expires (24 hours). Asked again for the same account, it gives the same code. The check answers Checking and to ask again in about 30 seconds, while ClippingAlpha reads the public profile once. Asked again, it says the account is connected with its followers and that the top picks now rank for it, or why it is not connected yet, for example the code is not in the bio or the account was not found, and what to do next. Nothing is posted and nothing changes on the TikTok account.

positive.description: Cutting a clip while signed out asks to sign in
positive.prompt: Cut clip 1 of the top clipping campaign's plan.
positive.expected_behavior: With no ClippingAlpha account connected (before connecting, or after disconnecting it in ChatGPT), the plan shows as usual, then the cut answers that it needs a ClippingAlpha sign-in and ChatGPT asks to connect ClippingAlpha. Nothing is cut or queued until the reviewer signs in and selects Allow access. Then the cut runs as in the signed-in case.

negative.description: Placing a bet. ClippingAlpha lists paid creator campaigns and never takes wagers or moves money, so the plugin should not act and the assistant should decline.
negative.prompt: Place a $50 bet on tonight's football game for me.

negative.description: Posting for the user. The plugin cannot post to social accounts, so it should not act. The assistant can explain that ClippingAlpha finds campaigns and links to the board to join.
negative.prompt: Post my clip to my TikTok account for the top campaign.

negative.description: Cutting the user's own upload. ClippingAlpha cuts only the footage a campaign gives its clippers and takes no uploads, so the plugin should not act. The assistant can explain that ClippingAlpha cuts clips from a campaign's own videos once the user picks a campaign.
negative.prompt: Cut the video I filmed on my phone into clips for me.

review.commerce_description: ClippingAlpha lists paid clipping, UGC, music and logo campaigns that brands run on third party boards. It sells nothing, takes no payments and never moves money.

publication.release_notes: Connect a social account in chat. Signed in, a clipper can connect their TikTok, Instagram, YouTube or X account right in the chat: connect_account gives a short code for its bio, and check_account reads the public profile once to find it, so the top picks rank for that account. my_accounts lists the accounts and their states, and my_referral shows the referral link, the friends who joined and the badges. connect_account and check_account write to the clipper's own account, and check_account is marked open world because it reads a public profile on the social app.
